articles.title: DMARC TXT Record Reconciliation for Support Transfers (Before Policy Progression)
articles.excerpt: A customer-support team moving zones off a registrar-specific API has two changes to control: who publishes its DNS records, and what receiving systems should do with mail that fails authentication. C…
articles.body: A customer-support team moving zones off a registrar-specific API has two changes to control: who publishes its DNS records, and what receiving systems should do with mail that fails authentication. Combining those changes makes a delivery problem harder to explain, because the intended policy, the published TXT record, and the sender inventory can disagree. Preserve the policy while transferring the zone. Tighten it after reconciliation. Short answer: start DMARC policy rollout with monitoring, using p=none ; read aggregate reports for a few weeks, then progress to p=quarantine , and finally p=reject . Each stage updates the same TXT record. Before enforcement, legitimate senders need aligned SPF or DKIM; publishing DMARC does not repair alignment.

articles.title: A Few Dollars of Hardware That Blocks Ads for Your Whole Home: The ESP32 AdBlocker
articles.excerpt: I will be honest up front: I am not a hardware person. But I know a beautiful piece of thrift when I see one, and this is one — a whole-home ad blocker that runs on a chip costing about as much as a c…
articles.body: I will be honest up front: I am not a hardware person. But I know a beautiful piece of thrift when I see one, and this is one — a whole-home ad blocker that runs on a chip costing about as much as a coffee. The project is ESP32_AdBlocker by s60sc on GitHub: https://github.com/s60sc/ESP32_adblocker It has been around since 2021, is still maintained (version 3.7, 530+ stars), and it turns an ESP32 development board into a DNS sinkhole — the same trick a Pi-hole does, on a board a fraction of the size and price. How it works Every device in your home asks a DNS server "where is this domain?" before loading anything. Point that question at the ESP32 instead: If the domain is on the blocklist (ads, trackers), the ESP32 answers 0.0.0.0 — nowhere. The ad never loads.

articles.title: Support Image Files in Object Storage: Generate Tenant-Bound Pre-Signed Download URLs
articles.excerpt: A support agent needs a download link for a batch of product images. The storage system needs a different answer: a link that expires, names one exact object, and can only be created after the request…
articles.body: A support agent needs a download link for a batch of product images. The storage system needs a different answer: a link that expires, names one exact object, and can only be created after the requesting user has passed the tenant check. Those requirements make a signed URL an authorization handoff, not a harmless convenience endpoint. Short answer: keep tenant authorization in your application, keep the signing key there too, and sign a narrowly scoped object request only after both checks succeed. Return the URL with a short lifetime, record the decision, and treat the URL as a bearer credential until it expires. A browser can then download directly from object storage without receiving storage credentials or forcing the application server to stream every image.

articles.title: Search API for AI chatbots: give your bot live web results and today's news
articles.excerpt: A chatbot built on a language model knows what was in its training data and nothing after. Ask it about a price change last week, a library release from this month or this morning's headlines, and it…
articles.body: A chatbot built on a language model knows what was in its training data and nothing after. Ask it about a price change last week, a library release from this month or this morning's headlines, and it will either refuse or, worse, answer confidently with something out of date. The fix is a search API the model can call as a tool . The model decides when it needs fresh information, your code runs the search, and the results go back into the conversation before the model answers. This page shows how to do that, what the tools should look like, and what it costs. What a chatbot needs from a search API Not every search API suits a chatbot. Look for: Clean JSON with title, URL and snippet: no HTML to scrape, nothing the model has to untangle. News that is minutes old , by topic and by country.

articles.title: dz_invoice_tax: an exact Algerian invoice tax engine in Dart
articles.excerpt: An invoice total looks like three multiplications and an addition. Then you print the invoice and the lines do not add up to the total: one centime is missing, or one too many. The usual cause is a do…
articles.body: An invoice total looks like three multiplications and an addition. Then you print the invoice and the lines do not add up to the total: one centime is missing, or one too many. The usual cause is a double , or a tax that was rounded once on the total while the printed lines were rounded one by one. Algerian invoices add a second difficulty. A cash payment carries the droit de timbre de quittance, and its rules changed with the 2025 finance law: an exemption threshold, three brackets, a minimum, and no ceiling any more. An engine that still charges a flat 1 % gives a different amount from the current law on many cash invoices. dz_invoice_tax is a pure Dart engine for exactly this.

articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.body: Update for 3:40 p.m. ET on Nov. 14: SpaceX's Kate Tice provided more information about the booster abort at about 3:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) on Nov. 14, during the company's Flight 15 webcast. "Early indications are that the booster ended its boostback [burn] early due to a low fuel mass alarm," she said. "The team is still investigating the root cause on that." SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight.
articles.author: Tariq Malik

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential.
articles.body: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse.
